jurisdiction: City of Green River, Emery County, UT
code_name: Green River City Code, Title 10 Zoning (Ch. 4 Establishment of Zones; Ch. 5 Agricultural; Ch. 6 Residential; Ch. 7 Commercial; Ch. 8 Industrial; Ch. 9 Open Space; Ch. 11-13 General, Supplementary, Conditional Uses; Ch. 17 Overlay Zones; Ch. 19 Redevelopment Overlay Zone)
edition: Zoneomics mirror of the Green River, UT zoning code (zoneomics.com/code/green-river-UT/chapter_N), read 2026-11-04; amendments seen include Ord. 2007-03, 2011-02, 2021-02, 2023-01 and 2025-01 (Ch. 18). NOT the official American Legal text.
caveats: Official American Legal code library returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch; every district below comes from the Zoneomics mirror only, so all districts should be treated as 'check source'. The mirror pages were read through a summarizing fetch, not as raw text, so wording is paraphrased and small details (footnotes, table cells) may have been lost. Confirm with Green River City Hall / planning before relying on it.

The code names the open space district OS-1 (Ch. 9). Our zoning layer labels it O-1; the O-1 entry below is the OS-1 text and the mapping O-1 = OS-1 is an assumption (the code lists no district called O-1).

The code names the overlay 'Sp-1 Special Overlay' (10-4-1). RDA corresponds to the 'Redevelopment Overlay Zone' (Ch. 19). Neither is a use zone. The RDA label is matched by name only; the code text never lists the redevelopment areas or their boundaries.

Title 10 appears to have no district-specific definitions for data center, solar farm, explosives, hazardous manufacturing, outdoor storage, truck terminal or heavy industry (Ch. 2 definitions only returned extractive industry, mineral processing and sight obscuring in the search; the full Chapter 2 was not read line by line). Treat them as 'not addressed' unless a use appears in the matrices below.

Under 10-11-5 any use not expressly permitted in a zone is prohibited, unless the board finds it similar to a permitted use. The industrial matrix (10-8-2) lists only 18 uses, so data centers, explosives/energetics, battery/chemical plants and utility-scale solar are not listed and would need a similarity finding or a rezone / code amendment.

Industrial districts state no minimum lot area, no minimum width, no height limit and no lot coverage limit (10-8-3, -4, -6). Only a 25 ft setback from the easement line (10-8-5) is stated; the mirror says the setback may be increased by use with Uniform Fire Code distances recommended. Chapter 12 (10-12-6) lets buildings exceed zone height limits if fire service can reach them and they are set back 1 ft per extra foot of height.
Lot coverage is not addressed in any district chapter read (A-1, R-1 to R-3, C-1, C-2, I-1 to I-3, OS-1).
C-1/C-2 lot area is shown as 'see below' with no values in the mirror; C-1/C-2 rear setback is 'A' (administrative); heights are 8 ft minimum and 35 ft maximum with fire marshal increases.

Green River city limits and the SP-1 area are described as being mainly west of the irrigation canal (expansive Mancos shale soils). Which base districts SP-1 parcels carry is not stated in the code; check the zone map held by the City Recorder (10-4-2).

Ch. 10 (Developments), Ch. 14 (Signs), Ch. 15-16 (Administration, Violations), the full Ch. 2 definitions and the title page were not read. G-1 Grazing exists in the code but is not requested and is not documented here.

districts.name: Medium Industrial
districts.purpose: Medium industry that buffers heavy industry from other zones; uses may be somewhat noisier or smellier than I-1 and produce fewer contaminants than heavy industry.
permitted_uses: Asphalt mixing plants
Automobile salvage and wrecking yards (screened)
Coal yards
Grazing livestock and related agricultural buildings
Impound lots (screened)
Incidental retailing tied to permitted industrial uses
Public buildings and utility facilities
Repair and craft shops
Towers and high-voltage power lines
Trucking dispatch, loading and docking depots
Warehouse and storage facilities
conditional_uses: Petroleum refining and related facilities are governed by conditional-use criteria in 10-13-5(L); the mirror does not show which district matrix lists them

standards.min_lot_size: None stated (enough area for setbacks, parking, loading and access)
standards.setbacks: Buildings at least 25 ft from the easement line; may be increased by use, Uniform Fire Code distances recommended
standards.other: No minimum width. Cargo containers allowed as accessory storage, stacking limit waived (10-18-4). Pollution limits in 10-12-16. Loading spaces and 1 parking space per 2,000 sq ft for manufacturing / warehouse (10-12-13).

districts.notes: Explosives / energetics / hazardous manufacturing: not addressed (not a listed use; not permitted unless the board finds it similar to a listed use under 10-11-5). Data center: not addressed. Solar farm: not addressed as a use; 'commercial power generation plants' is conditional and 10-13-5(J) sets conditions for small wind/solar (small-scale, 20 kW). Outdoor storage: salvage and impound yards (screened), coal yards and warehouse / storage facilities are permitted; screening required for yards, otherwise no general outdoor-storage rule found. Truck terminal: trucking dispatch / loading / docking depots are permitted (a separate 'truck terminal' use is prohibited in C-1/C-2 only). Strongest industrial fit of the three for heavy or messy uses without a conditional permit, but still not a fit for energetics by right.

districts.name: Light Industrial
districts.purpose: Light manufacturing, processing, warehousing and fabrication with minimal impact on neighbors; a buffer between medium/heavy industry and other zones. Quiet, low-odor, low-traffic uses with little airborne contamination.
permitted_uses: Grazing livestock and related agricultural buildings
Impound lots (screened)
Public buildings and utility facilities
Repair and craft shops
Trucking dispatch, loading and docking depots
Warehouse and storage facilities
conditional_uses: Incidental retailing tied to permitted industrial uses

standards.setbacks: Buildings at least 25 ft from the easement line; may be increased by use
standards.other: No minimum width. Cargo containers allowed as accessory storage (10-18-4).

districts.notes: Not allowed in I-1: automobile salvage / wrecking yards, coal yards, commercial power generation plants, slaughterhouses, sexually oriented businesses, landfills. Explosives / hazardous manufacturing, data center, solar farm: not addressed (commercial power generation is N here). Outdoor storage limited to screened impound lots and warehouse / storage. Trucking depots permitted.

districts.name: Heavy Industrial
districts.purpose: Heavy industry that is noisier, generates more traffic and produces more contaminants; primary purpose is manufacturing, processing, warehousing and fabrication of goods and materials.
permitted_uses: Asphalt mixing plants
Automobile salvage and wrecking yards (screened)
Coal yards
Food processing plant
Grazing livestock and related agricultural buildings
Impound lots (screened)
Incidental retailing tied to permitted industrial uses
Extractive industry
Mineral processing
Public buildings and utility facilities
Repair and craft shops
Slaughterhouse / meat processing plant
Towers and high-voltage power lines
Trucking dispatch, loading and docking depots
Warehouse and storage facilities

standards.setbacks: Buildings at least 25 ft from the easement line; may be increased by use, Uniform Fire Code distances recommended
standards.other: No minimum width. Cargo containers allowed as accessory storage (10-18-4; the mirror lists the heavy zone as '3'). Petroleum refining criteria in 10-13-5(L) include 1,000 ft separation of residential development from industrial uses.

districts.notes: Broadest permitted list (extractive industry and mineral processing by right). Explosives / energetics / hazardous manufacturing: not addressed as a listed use; would need a similarity finding under 10-11-5 or an amendment. Data center: not addressed. Solar farm: not addressed as such; commercial power generation plants are conditional. Outdoor storage: salvage, impound and coal yards allowed (screened where noted). Truck terminal: trucking depots permitted. Best code fit in the city for heavy uses, with no height or coverage limits.

districts.name: Open Space (code name OS-1)
districts.purpose: Areas where development should be limited or excluded for health, safety and welfare, typically riverbeds, floodplains and undeveloped land without extended public utilities; should not be urbanized unless first amended to another zone.
permitted_uses: Agriculture (row crops, grains, fruit, incidental buildings)
Non-supplemental livestock grazing on BLM open range allotments
Public facilities: parks, campgrounds, recreation developments with no dwellings, golf courses, utility substations, water storage, sewage treatment
conditional_uses: Limited raising and keeping of animals or fowl in barns, pens, coops
Private recreational facilities with no dwelling units

standards.other: Area, width, height, location, building size and special provisions are set by the planning commission when conditional use approval is granted.

districts.notes: No industrial, warehouse, solar, data center or storage uses listed; all not addressed, so prohibited under 10-11-5. The code has no district named O-1; mapped to OS-1 as an assumption. Floodplain / riverbed intent makes it a poor site for any campus.

districts.name: Special Overlay Zone (expansive soils)
districts.purpose: Overlay covering Green River areas with expansive soils (Mancos shale, fine-grained clay), mainly west of the irrigation canal, where swelling and shrinking soil can crack foundations. The code gives guidelines, not a use list.

standards.other: Suggested guidelines (10-17A-1): a soils report from a Utah-licensed civil or soils engineer (test holes, moisture, bearing pressure, expansion potential); the zoning administrator or building inspector may require added tests or foundation design; direct rain and irrigation water away from foundations. Floating adjustable piers suggested.

districts.notes: SP-1 is an overlay, not a use zone: it creates no permitted or conditional uses and sets no mandatory standards in the text read. The base districts it sits on are not stated (null); use the zone map (10-4-2) or the parcel's own base zoning. For scoring: treat as a geotechnical flag (foundation cost / soils report), not as a use signal. A parcel labeled only SP-1 has no known permitted-use list in the code.

districts.name: Agricultural
districts.purpose: Crop cultivation, livestock raising and related uses; agriculture takes priority; large lots and tracts mixed with dwellings.
permitted_uses: Agriculture (row and forage crops, grains, fruit, incidental farm buildings)
Raising animals and fowl (no porcine or ratites); barns, corrals, pens, farm storage at least 50 ft from dwellings
State-approved daycare nurseries; fairgrounds, equestrian centers, golf courses
Single-family dwellings, individual manufactured homes
Kennels, veterinary clinics, animal hospitals; plant nurseries; beehives
Public utility buildings and facilities, airports
Rest homes, schools, churches
Temporary construction storage yards (up to 1 year, two 90-day renewals)
Retail sale of products the owner raises
conditional_uses: Industry (planning commission recommendation and city council approval; permit not transferable between sites)
Water reservoirs, water facilities, oil and gas wells

standards.min_lot_size: 16,000 sq ft per dwelling (7,500 sq ft if on public sewer); 29,000 sq ft with animals; 1 acre for rest homes, schools, churches; no other area requirement
standards.setbacks: Front 25 ft from easement line; side 6 ft (16 ft combined) for dwellings; corner street side 25 ft; rear 30 ft for main buildings, 6 ft accessory; 10 ft between main and accessory buildings
standards.other: Lot width 70 ft (80 ft corner) for dwellings, none for other uses. Cargo containers allowed as accessory storage with no stacking limit (10-18-4).

districts.notes: 'Industry' is a conditional use with no definition or use list in the mirror, so heavy or hazardous industry, data centers and solar could only be sought by conditional use permit; each is otherwise not addressed. The code does not define what 'industry' includes. Outdoor storage: only temporary construction storage yards by right. Utility-scale solar: not addressed. Sibling district G-1 Grazing (5 acre minimum; quarries, gravel pits, cement mixing by right) is not documented here.

districts.name: Redevelopment Overlay Zone
districts.purpose: Flexible land use in city-established redevelopment areas where existing patterns and uses do not meet community standards (existing facilities, undersized lots, blighted areas); a conditional use permit may reduce parking or modify requirements for uses that benefit the area.
conditional_uses: Every use in the overlay is a conditional use requiring a conditional use permit; existing uses may continue or change, buildings may be altered, and uses may be limited in scope or duration

standards.min_lot_size: Same as the underlying zone unless modified by conditional use permit after a public hearing
standards.max_height: Same as the underlying zone unless modified
standards.setbacks: Same as the underlying zone unless modified
standards.lot_coverage: Same as the underlying zone unless modified
standards.other: The municipal redevelopment agency must get timely notice of each application.

districts.notes: Overlay, not a use zone: no uses by right ('None', 10-19-2). The base districts and the mapped redevelopment areas are not stated in the text (null). For scoring: treat as an entitlement-risk flag (every use needs a conditional use permit and public hearing) and read the underlying base zone from the zone map; do not assume any use is allowed. Labeling RDA = 'Redevelopment Overlay Zone' is by name only.

districts.name: Low Density Residential
districts.purpose: Primarily one- and two-family housing with parks, schools, churches and community facilities; spacious lots and quiet conditions. Newly annexed land is classified R-1 until rezoned (10-11-7).
permitted_uses: Single-family dwellings, individual modular homes, accessory buildings and private garages
Agriculture; private greenhouses and gardens; swimming pools
Public parks, schools, churches
Temporary construction storage (up to 1 year, two 90-day renewals)
conditional_uses: Rest homes and daycare nurseries designed as homes
Two-family dwellings (duplexes) designed to look like single-family homes

standards.setbacks: Front 25 ft from easement line (may match neighbors); side 8 ft; corner street side 25 ft; rear 15 ft main building, 6 ft accessory
standards.other: Lot width 70 ft (80 ft corner); minimum ground floor 700 sq ft.

districts.notes: No industrial, storage, solar or data center uses; all not addressed. Parcels in our data labeled R-1 may be newly annexed, un-rezoned land (10-11-7), so the label may not reflect intended use.

districts.name: Commercial (C-1)
districts.purpose: Retail, commercial and service facilities for residents and the traveling public; predominantly commercial with limited dwellings.
permitted_uses: Retail, restaurants, bars, banks, offices, hotels and motels, gas stations, automobile sales, car washes, medical and assembly uses
Bus terminal, taxi
Candy manufacture (non-industrial, in-shop retail); indoor sign manufacture
conditional_uses: Auto repair, towing and impound yards, wholesale business, cabinet shop, welding shop, ministorage, tire sales
Single-family homes, mixed-use residential, caretaker quarters

standards.max_height: 35 ft (8 ft minimum); may be increased with Fire Marshal approval
standards.setbacks: Front 0, side 0, corner street side 0 (subject to Unified Fire Code and Fire Marshal approval); rear administrative
standards.other: Merchandise and equipment must be stored inside a building or enclosure; enclosures within 75 ft of a residence must be sight-obscuring (10-7A-4).

districts.notes: Truck terminal, junkyards, materials recycling, wind turbines: not allowed. Data center, solar, explosives manufacturing: not addressed.

districts.name: Commercial (C-2, interstate)
districts.purpose: Agriculture, commercial storage, industrial warehouses and advertising sign display next to the interstate freeway, but not at on- or off-ramps; allows storage and warehouses in a non-residential area.
permitted_uses: Everything permitted in C-1, plus agriculture accessory buildings, beehives, equestrian centers, fairgrounds, golf courses
Auto repair and storage (enclosed), towing and impound yards (fenced), tire sales, parts sales
Wholesale business, building materials and lumberyard, cabinet, welding, farm implement, trailer sales, monument works
Moving and storage company, ministorage and self-storage, RV storage, RV parks
Stadium, arena, water park, boarding of small animals
conditional_uses: Ball fields, boarding of large animals, kennels
Sign manufacture or painting (outdoor), auction and swap meets, landscape rock sales yard

standards.max_height: 35 ft (8 ft minimum); may be increased with Fire Marshal approval
standards.setbacks: Front 0, side 0, corner street side 0 (Unified Fire Code, Fire Marshal approval); rear administrative
standards.other: Outdoor merchandise and equipment storage must be enclosed; hard-surfaced parking; landscape standards in 10-7A-6.

districts.notes: Truck terminal, junkyards, materials recycling, wind turbines: not allowed. Data center, solar, explosives manufacturing: not addressed. Warehousing and storage are the stated district purpose.

districts.name: Residential (manufactured / modular homes)
districts.purpose: Residential environment typified by modular and manufactured homes (HUD code units built on or after June 15, 1976) that blends with surrounding neighborhoods.
permitted_uses: Single-family dwellings, individual manufactured homes, accessory buildings
Agriculture, parks, schools, churches, temporary construction storage
conditional_uses: Multiple-family dwellings, duplexes, mobile home parks

standards.setbacks: Front 20 ft; side 8 ft; corner street side 25 ft; rear 15 ft main, 6 ft accessory

districts.notes: No industrial, solar or data center use; not addressed.

districts.name: Residential (high density)
districts.purpose: Variety of dwelling types at higher density and traffic; multiple-family dwellings have priority.
permitted_uses: Apartments, condominiums, single-family, townhomes, two-family dwellings
Childcare nurseries, foster group homes, nursing and rest homes, orphanages
Manufactured homes, churches, schools, public parks, accessory structures, agriculture
conditional_uses: Privately owned amusement or recreation parks
Retail businesses incidental to multiple-family buildings

standards.min_lot_size: 5,000 sq ft plus 600 sq ft per additional dwelling unit
standards.setbacks: Front 20 ft; side 8 ft; corner street side 25 ft; rear 15 ft main, 6 ft accessory

districts.notes: No industrial, solar or data center use; not addressed.
